posts.author: Nenen
posts.body:
I used to not like horror much, played a little of Witch's house and was too creeped out, a tad of various other games too but didn't get far in any.
Then I played
Midnight Train
(by lydiabluebell going by her itch handle)
The story hooked me in. Waiting for the next episode release was kinda fun too in a way, gave me time to think about the story.
Later, a discord server I was part of had an RM "book club" where we'd play a game and provide our thoughts afterwards.
And the game that was picked first was
Pocket Mirror
(classic) by astralshift, this was one of the games I barely played before, but this time I had an extra push to play it.
They're both now some of my favorites, and I'm now willing to give those other games a try (when ever I have time and energy for it
)

posts.author: socon
posts.body:
misterweirddumbass said:
That one does seem disturbing and whimsy at the same time, what can you tell me about it?
Click to expand...
It's surprisingly poetic from the plot to the art really. Watching a child experience such unnatural tragic things is heartbreaking due to the fact that he doesn't understand most of what's happening. The writing is so good lol, lines like "I'm not afraid of what I'm able to stab but I can't stab darkness" hit so hard. I think it's a horror in the most unconventional way.

posts.author: Prescott
posts.body:
I played a game called Lurking Under Life in RPG Maker XP as a kid. Scared me so much but it's not that bad now. It was never technically finished, but someone on this forum managed to scrounge it up randomly and it is now backed up to archive.org. You can see the thread for that here:
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/threads/lost-media-lurking-under-life.161246/
